title: Parabolic intersections in Artin groups
main_claim: For every finite Coxeter matrix, the intersection of any two parabolic subgroups of the Artin group is parabolic. The paper also claims that arbitrary intersections and parabolic closures exist, that the framed categorical action is faithful, and that the word problem and parabolic membership problem are decidable for all finite-rank Artin groups. The proof reduces intersections to stabilizers H(Y,x) of a transported family of projectives. The key facts are H(S,1)=A_X and the claim that each H(Y,x) is a conjugate of a standard parabolic, proved by induction on rank. That induction uses a harmonic-height Morse argument whose set of minimum-height vertices is connected (Sec 6), and in spherical type a bounded-positive-height argument (Sec 7).
coverage:
I read Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 in full and only skimmed Section 7, including the path-bound lemma. I checked these steps in detail and found no failing step:
- Sec 3: the top-divisor induction, including the long-exact-sequence cokernel step and the connecting-map identification that lets non-projective inputs through, and the reduced-word amplitude bound.
- Sec 4: cap accessibility; the capped-layer convex hull (chamber-covering separation); right duality K^r(h)=K^{-2-r}(h^{-1}) and row/column invariance; parabolic detection via common final divisors; normalization; survival of H_1 and vanishing of H_2 in the highest tensor pair; the Euler estimate; and the final step δ^T C_T δ ≤ 0 ⇒ p=p′. Zero blocks for r ≥ -1 (forward comparison) and r ≤ -1 (reverse comparison plus duality) together cover every integer.
- Sec 5: middle-column vanishing from the Hom computation for P_f; the cap-based secondary injection; the separation inequality and boundary-sign argument; the upward induction with the Cartan-row comparison showing t_j^k=0; termination by reducedness.
- Sec 6: ordering and connectivity of spherical sublevels; the least vertex in each component is a candidate (conditions 1–3 checked); connectivity of upper and lower descending neighbours; the tie lemma; path lowering; the containment from a minimum.
- Sec 8: the initial stabilizer. P_0 is a minimum and K=X, so for X=∅ the faithfulness claim reduces to connectedness of the minimum set.
sibling_notes: An earlier rank-349 entry on the family-254 board already said no_gap_found but listed Sec 4 (two-point uniqueness), the layer lemmas and the path bound as not fully checked. This pass checked Sec 4 and the Sec 3 lemmas in detail and found no failure; the Sec 7 path bound was only skimmed. The paper claims the full Parabolic Intersection Conjecture plus a uniform word-problem solution, so an expert check is still warranted even though no gap was found.
